official_source_candidates.fact: The 2026 Planned Network Deployments report is based on operator plans stated as of January 2026; It forecasts deployment over the following three years to the end of 2028 or January 2029; The Spring 2026 Connected Nations update is the separate January 2026 snapshot of existing coverage
official_source_candidates.guard: Store plan-vintage, forecast horizon and observed-coverage snapshot separately; never promote planned deployment to current availability.

official_source_candidates.fact: A plan is High Confidence only when it has reached at least Low Level Design Complete; Funding must also have been committed; Planning maturity alone or funding alone is insufficient
official_source_candidates.guard: Require both documented conditions for High Confidence and retain lower-confidence plans separately.

official_source_candidates.fact: Ofcom publishes outcomes for all stated plans and separately for High Confidence plans; The scenarios produce different projected coverage percentages; Neither scenario is a guarantee that build will be completed
official_source_candidates.guard: Keep all-plan and High-Confidence scenario columns distinct and label both as forecasts rather than realised coverage.

official_source_candidates.fact: Key findings refer to residential properties only; A separate local-authority file provides results for all premises including residential and business
official_source_candidates.guard: Require population-scope metadata on every planned-deployment metric and reject residential/all-premises substitution.

official_source_candidates.fact: Projected residential coverage percentages use the same premise base as the Spring 2026 update; That base contains 30.5 million residential premises
official_source_candidates.guard: Pin the 30.5 million January 2026 residential denominator for published scenario reconciliation; do not silently replace it with a later address epoch.

official_source_candidates.fact: Some planned build adds coverage while other plans overbuild existing or other planned networks; Ofcom estimates homes with access to at least two and at least three gigabit-capable networks
official_source_candidates.guard: Deduplicate premises for coverage while retaining provider/network multiplicity; provider-plan totals must not be summed as unique premises.

official_source_candidates.fact: About 6950 additional geographically distinct FWA masts are planned or set for upgrade between January 2026 and January 2029; The mast count describes planned infrastructure rather than a verified premise-coverage count
official_source_candidates.guard: Do not convert mast counts into served premises, parcels or coverage percentages without an official propagation and premise-matching model.

official_source_candidates.fact: The official known-data-issues page lists two STREET records with a start or end X or Y coordinate incorrectly set to 000000.00
official_source_candidates.guard: Quarantine zero STREET coordinates with issue provenance; do not treat them as valid origins, delete the street, or generalise the issue to every zero-valued field.

official_source_candidates.fact: The productVersionInfo endpoint returns current valid version information for a requested correlation method; The correlation method path parameter is restricted to the eleven documented relationships
official_source_candidates.guard: Use API results only as current-state evidence; they cannot prove the byte identity or source versions of a retained historical download.

official_source_candidates.fact: The Linked Identifiers API requires an API key or OAuth2 token; Documented responses distinguish malformed request, unauthenticated, forbidden, not found, rate limited, server error and temporary outage
official_source_candidates.guard: Preserve HTTP status and retry class; never convert 401, 403, 429 or 503 into an empty relationship result.

official_source_candidates.fact: Download delivery contains eleven complete relationship packages with CSV, versions JSON, licence and description; The API exposes identifier queries and current product-version information
official_source_candidates.guard: Do not use API query success as proof that all download packages, historical epochs, row counts or package hashes were validated.

official_source_candidates.fact: The great majority of registered titles use the general-boundaries rule; Title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is shown as determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002; There is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between a general title-plan boundary and the legal boundary
official_source_candidates.guard: Default every title-plan or index-polygon edge to general-boundary evidence unless an explicit determined-boundary register record is proven.

official_source_candidates.fact: A determined boundary records the exact line of a registered-estate boundary; The register identifies the affected boundary as determined and retains the determined-boundary plan; A title plan alone shows only the general position of the determined boundary
official_source_candidates.guard: Promote exact-boundary status only with matching register and determined-plan evidence; geometry appearance or survey precision alone is insufficient.

official_source_candidates.fact: A legal boundary is an exact imaginary line and is rarely identified precisely; A physical feature such as a fence, wall or hedge may or may not follow it; The legal boundary is not shown on Ordnance Survey mapping
official_source_candidates.guard: Keep legal boundary, physical feature and OS mapped feature as separate entities; never infer legal ownership from feature coincidence.

official_source_candidates.fact: A boundary agreement can be recorded in the register; Unless determined under section 60, the boundary remains a general boundary; The registrar does not guarantee that the legal boundary is where the agreement identifies it
official_source_candidates.guard: Do not promote a recorded boundary agreement to determined or exact status without the section-60 determination evidence.

official_source_candidates.fact: A title plan supports the property description and identifies the general extent of registered land; There are no title plans for relating franchises and lordship titles
official_source_candidates.guard: Classify a missing title plan for these documented title types as a scope exception rather than unregistered land, missing data corruption or no title.
